title: The US Govt took 10% of Intel for $8.9B in grants the govt had already promised
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Xebec
Well-known member

Interesting:

<partial excerpt>:

$8.9bn in grants for 10% of Intel
Under the deal, the government released $8.9 billion in grants that Intel had already won. Most came from the CHIPS Act. In return, the government took about 10% of Intel’s stock for free, WIRED reported. Shapiro told the company to weigh the value of having the administration on its side, including with customers.

The board’s minutes record doubts about the offer.

“The economic terms that had been proposed [by] the Administration were not, in their current form, attractive to the company,” the minutes say.

Click to expand...

The directors approved the deal two days later. That day, Trump posted on Truth Social that the US had paid nothing for the shares. He valued them at about $11 billion.

The pressure began earlier that month. Trump called on Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over his ties to China. Tan then met Trump in the Oval Office on 11 August 2025.
..
Intel shareholder Richard Paisner alleges that the board “caved to the government’s extortion.” Intel’s lawyers reject that account. In a motion to dismiss, they argue the board did negotiate. They say it won better terms, including the immediate release of the grants, WIRED reported.

‘Rejection will have consequences’: Commerce’s push for an Intel stake

Intel gave the US a 10% stake for $8.9bn in grants it had already won, court documents show. A judge hears the case on 10 December.
